item.title: RSA is hard because factoring is hard, Quantum computing changes that!
item.description: Was reading about some quantum computing concepts today and stumbled upon Shor's Algorithm and Grover's Algorithm. I've always been curious about how quantum computing could threaten modern cryptography. Got to know that RSA's security basically relies on the fact that multiplying two large primes is easy, but finding the original primes from the result is extremely hard. Shor's Algorithm changes that by making factorization efficient on a quantum computer. Grover's Algorithm was interesting too.
